notes: Configuration for the shared `test-audit` tool (tools/test-audit). Paths are relative to this file.

Feature selections are the coverage contract: `remote` transitively enables `network`; `network` alone cfg-outs `sniff::remote` and silently empties its Wiremock suites. `lib-bare` and `lib-network` are captured to show what those selections do NOT list.

`test-fixtures` on sniff-cli is L2-only locally (gates the real-terminal helper binaries); CI and `test-l2` enable it. Local L1 leaves it off, so `cli-bare` and `cli-fixtures` are distinct L1 populations.

Families (families.json) are declared in Phase 2 of the sniff fix: deterministic (fixture-owned inputs), native-detector (real platform APIs, cfg-gated, kept separate from deterministic cost), and real-resource (`real_`, `test-real`).
The sanity cohort is timed separately against its 15-second fast-confidence budget.

Counter readings carry `requestShape` (the DetectionPlan/GitRequest/RepoRequest tier used), `counterVersion` (sniff/lib/src/performance/counters.rs names are the contract), and `phase` (acquisition vs execution) so readings across different boundaries are never paired.
Native Windows and WSL2 are distinct environments (`platformKind`); WSL follows the Linux compile path.

routes.note: _sanity_all: sniff --features remote; sniff-cli --features test-fixtures; lib + bins, !slow; 15 s budget
_test_local_all: one invocation, sniff --features remote + sniff-cli (no test-fixtures)
sniff-cli --features test-fixtures; CI/CD status-cell and git-status styling
sniff --features network (real_ probes, skip-clean when absent); sniff-cli
local LCOV only; not a CI producer
work-counter table per OS; the counter evidence source
no local mingw check recipe; windows-latest is the Windows compile and runtime authority
